---
title: "codewindow HTML Example"
format: html
filters:
  - codewindow
---

The same `.codewindow` syntax works in plain HTML documents. Add the filter rather than the reveal plugin:

``` yaml
filters:
  - codewindow
```

## Basic usage

::: {.codewindow}
```scss
.pink {
  color: pink;
}
```
:::

## File name and icon

::: {.codewindow .sass}
styles.scss
```scss
.pink {
  color: pink;
}
```
:::

## Setting width

::: {.codewindow .sass width="350px"}
styles.scss
```scss
.pink {
  color: pink;
}
```
:::

## Setting colors

::: {.codewindow .sass bg="#fdf6e3" header-bg="#eee8d5" shadow-color="#93a1a1"}
styles.scss
```scss
.pink {
  color: pink;
}
```
:::

## Window chrome

::: {.codewindow .r chrome="windows"}
script.R
```r
runif(1)
```
:::

::: {.codewindow .r chrome="none"}
script.R
```r
runif(1)
```
:::

## Dark windows

::: {.codewindow .sass .codewindow-dark}
styles.scss
```scss
.pink {
  color: pink;
}
```
:::

## Multiple blocks in one window

::: {.codewindow .r}
my-script.R
```r
runif(1)
```

Then some more code:

```r
runif(42)
```
:::

## Multiple tabs

Outside a slide deck there are no fragments to advance, so the tabs are clickable instead. Any `.fragment` class on an `.editor` is ignored.

:::: {.codewindow}
::: {.editor .r name="00-load.R"}
```r
data <- read.csv("my-data.csv")
```
:::

::: {.editor .r .active name="01-clean.R"}
```r
library(dplyr)
data <- filter(data, x > 0)
```
:::

::: {.editor .r name="02-plot.R"}
```r
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point()
```
:::
::::
